title: What I think about drill in teaching.
author: Jo Castelino
summary: Science teacher Jo Castelino reconsiders drill and rote learning, which she disliked after a childhood of stressful rote schooling in the Middle East. Her early UK teaching relied on discovery lessons, posters and model-making, and her students could not recall key facts such as the structure of a cell. Reading cognitive science convinced her that these lessons overloaded working memory and that unrecalled facts block later understanding of complex ideas like chemical bonding. She argues that drill and retrieval practice build the confidence and foundation on which schema grow, while insisting that her own childhood misery came from rote learning being the only thing she was taught, with no application. She closes with her husband's recollection that memorising the first 20 elements helped him massively.
points: Fun discovery lessons left her students unable to recall key facts, which she attributes to working-memory overload.
Secure recall of basic facts frees working memory for new technical terms, so students feel confident rather than lost and switched off.
Drill is a foundation for complex ideas, not the whole of a lesson.
The stress of her own schooling came from rote learning being all she was taught and the pressure on marks, not from the drill itself.
quotes: Since then, I have read a lot on cognitive science (check out these websites for more: the learning scientists and cogscisci). I realised that by using discovery/research/”fun” lessons, I was overloading my students’ working memories with the dreaded result of them not remembering most key facts. And if they could not remember those key facts, they could not then go on to understand more complex concepts.

Drill and rote learning have an important role to play in breeding success and motivation. I am not saying that every lesson and indeed the entire lesson is about getting students to repeat what I say or memorise key facts. But they are a foundation on which we can build complex ideas and schema to aid long-term learning.

My education was heavily focussed on remembering facts and chunks of information and not at all on application. Moving to the UK, I struggled at University because I didn’t really know how to apply any of what I had learnt.
